page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.u0.c1m2.xlarge is an entry-tier x86_64 server instance built on KVM hypervisor technology and powered by an Intel Xeon 8163 processor operating at 2.5 GHz. Configured with 2 physical cores and hyper-threading to deliver 4 dedicated vCPUs, the server provides 8.0 GB of system memory, yielding a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 2.0 GB per virtual CPU. Memory architecture includes 32 KB L1 data cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and a shared 33 MB L3 cache, with hardware support for AVX and AVX-512 instruction set extensions. The instance lacks local ephemeral storage and GPU hardware, relying entirely on network-attached block storage and offering a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Synthetic benchmark evaluations position the instance in the lower performance quartile across compute and memory subsystems. Stress-ng benchmarks record single-core and multi-core CPU metrics of 1105.28 and 2901.7 respectively, while Geekbench yields a single-core score of 948.0 and a multi-core score of 2039.0. Uncached large-block memory read bandwidth measures 19.91 GB/sec, and write bandwidth measures 18.49 GB/sec. Static web serving throughput reaches 2.54 GB/sec and PassMark CPU score records 3615.54. Qualitatively, the hardware profile offers an economical entry point for lightweight background processing, basic utility microservices, developmental testing environments, and low-traffic web applications where memory bandwidth demands remain low.

Equipped with 8.0 GB of RAM, it maintains a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio without local ephemeral storage or integrated GPU acceleration. Baseline network throughput is rated at 2 Gbps. Benchmark results place the instance in the lower performance tier across compute, memory bandwidth, and web serving tests, with Geekbench single-core and multi-core scores of 948.0 and 2039.0, and uncached memory read bandwidth of 19.91 GB/sec. Given its lean memory allocation and moderate hardware metrics, this instance provides a cost-effective environment for basic web applications, lightweight microservices, utility tasks, and development workloads that do not demand high memory capacity or intensive parallel processing.
